record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.context_brief: Projective invariance of geometric Poisson structures
record.original_question: Are geometric Poisson structures of every order greater than 1 projectively invariant, and can their leading coefficient g^{ij} always be interpreted as a projectively invariant weighted tensor of the appropriate weight?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1. Are geometric Poisson structures of any order greater than 1 projectively invariant? Can one interpret the leading coefficient gij as a projectively invariant object?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with a torsion-free affine connection $\nabla$. Two torsion-free connections $\nabla$ and $\widetilde{\nabla}$ on $M$ are said to be projectively equivalent if they share the same unparametrized geodesics; equivalently, there exists a 1-form $\omega$ on $M$ such that
$$\widetilde{\nabla}_X Y = \nabla_X Y + \omega(X)Y + \omega(Y)X$$
for all vector fields $X, Y$. A projective structure on $M$ is an equivalence class of such connections. A geometric tensor field of projective weight $w$ is a section of an appropriate density-twisted tensor bundle whose transformation rule under a change of projectively equivalent connections is governed by $\omega$ in the standard way.

For each integer $k \geq 1$, the "geometric Poisson structure of order $k$" on $M$ associated to a (pseudo-)Riemannian metric (or more generally to suitable geometric data) is a Poisson bracket on a function space on $M$ (in the formal/Hamiltonian formalism of hydrodynamic-type and higher-order systems) whose leading symbol in local coordinates is given by a contravariant tensor $g^{ij}$ accompanied by Christoffel-like coefficients, and which generalizes the Dubrovin–Novikov bracket (the case $k=1$).

Problem. Prove or disprove the following two assertions:

(a) For every integer $k > 1$, the geometric Poisson structure of order $k$ is projectively invariant, in the sense that it depends only on the projective class of the underlying connection.

(b) The leading coefficient $g^{ij}$ of every such geometric Poisson structure of order $k > 1$ admits an interpretation as a projectively invariant weighted tensor field of the appropriate projective weight.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned no results indicating a published proof or disproof of projective invariance for higher-order geometric Poisson structures or an interpretation of their leading coefficient as a projectively invariant weighted tensor. The question appears as an explicitly posed research problem in the area of Nijenhuis geometry and integrable systems, with no resolution located in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational paper on Nijenhuis geometry; does not address projective invariance of higher-order geometric Poisson structures.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the projective-invariance question for higher-order geometric Poisson structures is reported here.

status_evidence.title: Applications of Nijenhuis geometry: non-degenerate singular points of Poisson–Nijenhuis structures
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses local structure of Poisson-Nijenhuis pairs but not projective invariance of order-k geometric brackets.
status_evidence.claim: The cited literature on Poisson–Nijenhuis structures does not settle the stated problem.
